transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Well, what brings me in is that I just can’t seem to keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's like... I'll start talking about an overnight shift at work, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, and then paint colors, and then patient charts. I don't really mean to, but it just happens. And I can look at the people I'm talking to and see that everyone is getting completely lost. It's just making it really hard to communicate.
Can you tell me more about how your thoughts jump from one topic to another? Do you feel that your thoughts are connected or do they feel disjointed or unrelated to you?

Like I was just saying with the overnight shift and the paint colors... in my head, I guess it feels like they connect for a split second. Like one thing just triggers the next. But as soon as the words actually come out of my mouth, I realize they're completely unrelated. It's just disjointed. I don't mean to do it, but my brain just skips around, and that's why everyone at work ends up looking at me like they have no idea what I'm talking about.
Have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or had beliefs that others might find strange?

I haven't really heard voices or seen things like that. But... I guess I do have some thoughts that other people tell me are strange. 

Like at work, on the unit. I'm sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose, and I know they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. People keep telling me it's just because of staffing shortages, but... I know that's not true. I just know they're watching me.
Can you tell me more about your belief that the supervisors are watching you through the cameras? Do you feel they are doing this all the time or only at certain times?

It feels like it's all the time, honestly. Whenever I'm on the floor. I know they changed my shifts specifically so they could keep an eye on me. People keep saying, "Oh, it's just staffing shortages, we're short-handed," but... I know that's not it. I know they're watching me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. It's not just a feeling, I'm sure of it.
Do you ever doubt or question your belief that the supervisors are watching you through the cameras, or does it feel absolutely certain to you all the time?

I don't doubt it at all. It feels absolutely certain to me. Like I said, I'm just sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose, and they're watching me through those cameras to see if I'm unsafe. I know people keep trying to tell me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know what's really going on. I'm certain of it.
Has there ever been a time when you’ve questioned whether the cameras are really being used to watch you, or have you always felt completely sure about it with no doubt at all?

I've never questioned it. I mean, I know you're asking if I ever have doubts, but no, I don't. I'm completely sure they changed my shifts on purpose. I know they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. Everyone keeps saying it's just staffing shortages, but I know better. I've always been completely sure about it.
Can you tell me more about why you think the supervisors are watching you — do you feel they are trying to harm you or prevent you from doing something in particular?

I don't think they're trying to harm me, exactly. It's more like... they think I'm a risk or something. I'm sure they changed my shifts just so they could keep an eye on me when I'm on the floor. They watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. I know my coworkers and everyone else keep telling me it's just because of staffing shortages, but that's not true. They're watching me.

Have you ever had any evidence or experiences that made you reconsider your belief that the supervisors are watching you through the cameras, or has your belief stayed exactly the same regardless of what’s happened?

No, my belief has stayed exactly the same. I know I keep repeating myself, but nothing has made me reconsider. People try to give me reasons, like telling me it's just staffing shortages, but that doesn't change my mind. I'm just sure the supervisors changed my shifts and they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. That hasn't changed at all, regardless of what anyone says.

Even when people have given you specific reasons to doubt your belief — like explaining that shift changes are because of staffing shortages — has your belief stayed completely unchanged and unshakable?

Yeah, it's... it's completely unchanged. I know we've gone over this a few times now, but... no matter what anyone says about staffing shortages or whatever, I know the truth. I'm sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose. They're watching me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. That's just what's happening, and nothing they say is going to convince me otherwise.

When you're talking and your thoughts jump from one topic to another, do you have trouble organizing your thoughts so that your speech stays on topic, or do you feel like you're staying on track even if others don't see the connection?

I definitely have trouble organizing them. It's actually a big part of what brought me in, honestly. I just... I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. 

Like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts. I know I'm not staying on track, because I can literally see everyone getting lost while I'm speaking. It just comes out all over the place.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else or taken out, or is it more that your own thoughts just race or jump around on their own?

No, I don't feel like anyone is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. It's just... it's just my own thoughts. They just jump around on their own, like I said. I can't keep them organized, but they're definitely mine. No one else is messing with them inside my head.
Is your speech becoming disorganized and jumping from one topic to another happening all the time when you're talking, or does it only happen in certain situations or with certain people?

It's happening pretty much all the time now. Like I was just saying... that's really what brought me in, because I just can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore, no matter who I'm talking to. 

It doesn't matter if it's the other aides at work or just someone at home. I'll start explaining something about an overnight shift, and then I'm suddenly rambling about soccer, or paint colors, or the patient charts... and I can see everyone getting lost, every single time. So, yeah, it's not just in certain situations or with specific people. It's just happening all the time.
Have you ever experienced things like strange bodily sensations, illusions, or other unusual perceptions that aren't quite like hearing voices or seeing things, but still feel out of the ordinary?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. No weird sensations in my body or anything out of the ordinary like that. It's just the voices and the shadows, really. I don't get any strange feelings on my skin or illusions or whatever. Just what I've already mentioned.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs that other people might not understand or find strange, besides the belief that you are being watched through the cameras?

No, just the cameras. Well, and the shifts. I'm... I'm absolutely sure the supervisors are changing my shifts on purpose. They want to watch me through those unit cameras, to see if I'm, you know, unsafe or doing something wrong. People keep telling me it's just staffing shortages, that everyone's schedule is messed up right now, but I know that's not true. They're doing it to keep an eye on me. But besides that, no, nothing else.

Even though people have given you specific explanations, like shift changes being due to staffing shortages, have you completely dismissed those explanations as possibilities and still believed, without any doubt, that the only real reason is that they are watching you through the cameras?

Yeah, absolutely. I hear them saying it's just a staffing shortage, but... I don't believe that at all. Like I was saying, I am completely sure the supervisors changed my shifts specifically to watch me through the unit cameras. They want to see if I'm unsafe. So, yeah, I don't have any doubt about it, no matter what excuse they try to give me. I know exactly why they're doing it.

Even though people have explained that shift changes are due to staffing shortages, do you believe the only real reason is that supervisors are watching you through cameras, and do you feel completely certain with no room for doubt?

Yeah, I mean, I know we just talked about this, but yes. I am completely sure. People can tell me it's staffing shortages all they want, but I know the supervisors changed my shifts. They did it so they can watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. There's no doubt in my mind about it.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I maintain my belief despite contradictory evidence (staffing shortages), which directly relates to the fixed nature of delusions.

patient.answer: Yeah, absolutely. I hear them saying it's just a staffing shortage, but... I don't believe that at all. Like I was saying, I am completely sure the supervisors changed my shifts specifically to watch me through the unit cameras. They want to see if I'm unsafe. So, yeah, I don't have any doubt about it, no matter what excuse they try to give me. I know exactly why they're doing it.

doctor.intent: Assess the presence and nature of delusional beliefs, particularly whether the belief that supervisors are watching the patient through cameras is fixed, unshakable, and held with absolute certainty despite evidence to the contrary.
doctor.question: Even though people have explained that shift changes are due to staffing shortages, do you believe the only real reason is that supervisors are watching you through cameras, and do you feel completely certain with no room for doubt?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m sure the supervisors changed my shifts and watch me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe, even when people tell me it’s just staffing shortages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's firm belief that supervisors are watching them through cameras and changing their shifts, despite being given alternative explanations (staffing shortages). This directly corresponds to the 'Delusions' symptom.

patient.answer: Yeah, I mean, I know we just talked about this, but yes. I am completely sure. People can tell me it's staffing shortages all they want, but I know the supervisors changed my shifts. They did it so they can watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. There's no doubt in my mind about it.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent delusions regarding being watched by supervisors through cameras at work, with no accompanying prominent hallucinations or other symptoms characteristic of schizoaffective disorder. The delusions are non-bizarre, fixed, and unshakable, and they center around a plausible life context (workplace surveillance). There is no evidence of a major mood episode occurring concurrently with the delusions, which supports a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder (F22) over Schizoaffective Disorder (F25.0).
